extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, aviation industry stakeholders, operators, and practitioners tracking FAA Federal Register publications and rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: An index/listing of Federal Aviation Administration documents published on the Federal Register (notices, proposed rules, final rules, airworthiness directives, and special conditions), with abstracts, publication dates, and links. Useful for tracking rulemaking, information-collection notices, airspace changes, ADs, and related FAA actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act — public comment and OMB approval
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, FAA invites public comments about our intention to request the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) approval to renew an information collection. The Federal Register Notice with a 60-day comment period soliciting comments was published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices must solicit public comment (typically a 60-day comment period noted here) when FAA intends to request or renew OMB approval for information collections. Explanations should justify the need for the collection and provide OMB/administrative context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information collection — minimum required fields and voluntary submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The collection involves information voluntarily submitted (e.g., through the FAA Noise Portal); the required fields in the portal represent the minimum information necessary for the FAA to respond effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information collections should limit required fields to the minimum necessary to accomplish the stated purpose (prevent fragmented/delayed responses, enhance transparency, improve community engagement, and support centralized intake). Statements of voluntary submission and purpose should be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: New information collection — surface weather reporting content and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Collection involves voluntarily reporting when National Airspace System (NAS) surface weather systems (AWOS and ASOS) experience operational issues, such as erroneous data or full outages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collected reports must be usable to verify and track errors/outages and to publish status to the FAA's Surface Weather Status Dashboard for user awareness; notice should describe what will be collected and how it will be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information collection for airman certification (Flight Engineers and Navigators)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collection involves FAA Form 8400-3, Application for an Airman Certificate and/or Rating (for flight engineer and flight navigator) and applications for approval of related training courses submitted to FAA for evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The data collected are necessary to determine applicant eligibility for certificates and to determine training course acceptability; notices should explain how the information supports eligibility and course-approval determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction amendment to regulatory text
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rule contained typographical, grammatical, and formatting errors in sections of Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations; this document corrects those errors in the final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When final regulations contain textual errors, agencies issue correction amendments to fix typographical/grammatical/formatting mistakes. Corrections should identify the affected sections and the nature of the corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Airspace action justification and design criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions amending, establishing, modifying, or revoking Class D and Class E airspace (or jet routes and VOR Federal airways) are taken due to operational changes (e.g., abandoned heliport, canceled instrument procedures, NAVAID decommissioning, VOR MON program), to properly contain current IFR operations, and to provide enroute continuity with other authorities' route modernization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Airspace proposals/changes must be justified by concrete operational reasons (abandonment, canceled procedures, NAVAID decommissioning, modernization efforts). Legal descriptions must be updated to reflect current airport names, geographic coordinates, the FAA aeronautical database, and current FAA guidance (e.g., replace 'Airport/Facility Directory' with 'Chart Supplement'). Actions should demonstrate they support safety and management of IFR and VFR operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Airworthiness Directive (AD) requirements to address unsafe conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: ADs require revising existing maintenance or inspection programs to incorporate new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations; require inspections (e.g., general visual inspection, local thickness mapping, full panel thickness measurement), applicable corrective actions, and may add new airplane models to applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ADs are issued to address unsafe conditions and may supersede prior ADs, continue certain required actions, or impose new requirements. They may mandate specific inspections, measurements, corrective actions, revisions to programs, and inclusion of additional airplane models; documentation should state the unsafe condition and the required compliance actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: AD operational restrictions and procedural prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Some ADs impose operational restrictions (e.g., dispatch restrictions from using certain MMEL items) and prohibit use of certain maintenance tasks (e.g., SRM tasks) until unsafe conditions are addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ADs may include immediate operational limitations and prohibitions affecting dispatch or maintenance procedures; notices should explain the scope, affected items/tasks, and any interim measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADs with repetitive inspections and optional terminating actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed ADs may require repetitive inspections of affected parts and provide replacement as an optional terminating action; they may also limit or prohibit installation of affected parts under certain conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals for ADs should state inspection intervals, on-condition corrective actions, available terminating actions (and whether optional), and any installation limitations to prevent recurrence of the unsafe condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special conditions for novel or unusual design features
rubrics_metrics.description: When an aircraft (or modification) has a novel or unusual design feature not envisioned by existing airworthiness standards (e.g., four-axis full-authority digital fly-by-wire flight control system, rechargeable lithium-ion battery installations), the applicable regulations do not contain adequate safety standards; FAA issues special conditions containing additional safety standards necessary to establish an equivalent level of safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special conditions articulate additional safety requirements specific to the novel feature to achieve an equivalent level of safety. Notices should describe the novel feature, why existing rules are inadequate, and the additional safety standards being imposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flight manual and maintenance manual revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed or final actions may require revising existing manuals (e.g., rotorcraft flight manual, airworthiness limitations section of maintenance manuals) to address identified unsafe conditions or new maintenance/inspection requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When mandated, manual revisions must be specified (which section, the content to add/modify) and tied to compliance timelines; notices often require updating instructions for continued airworthiness and approved maintenance/inspection programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency AD issuance and required operational checks
rubrics_metrics.description: An AD may be issued as an emergency AD (previously sent to known U.S. owners/operators) prompted by in-service failures (e.g., pitch trim actuator failures). Such ADs require operational checks (e.g., of pitch trim actuator), provide verification options, and mandate on-condition actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency ADs are used where immediate action is needed; notices should document prior emergency communications, required checks, acceptable verification procedures, and follow-up corrective actions to ensure safety.
